etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English subverten, from Old French subvertir, from Latin subvertō (“to overthrow”, literally “to underturn, turn from beneath”).
senses: (transitive) To overturn from the foundation; to overthrow; to ruin utterly.
(transitive) To pervert, as the mind, and turn it from the truth; to corrupt; to confound.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: Back-formation from subvertising, by analogy with advert.
